prompt:
I need the front end for Chartpantry. A free community collection of reproducible chart recipes, with data, code and a written walkthrough for each, where hobbyists search for a way to show their own data and get suggestions based on what their dataset looks like.

Who's using it: Walter Pruitt, 67, a retired high-school earth science teacher in Fargo who volunteers with the county historical society. He knows some Python from a community-college class and makes charts on weekends for fun; this is his own project, not for the society.

What they're doing right now: Walter has a 127-year daily weather record for Fargo (high, low, precipitation, snow depth) that he cleaned up himself, and he wants to make one striking image for a poster showing how winters have changed. He's tried searching phrases like 'many years of daily temperature in one picture' and 'warming stripes but for winter only' and got a mix of hits, some close and some not. He just uploaded a sample of his file's columns so the site can suggest recipes that fit its shape, and now he has to decide which two or three candidates are worth trying, keeping in mind he can't install anything beyond Python and matplotlib.

What's in the system at this point: Collection: 8,400 recipes. Each has: title (e.g., 'Daily temperature ribbon, 1950–2020, Toronto'), author handle, tools used (matplotlib, ggplot2, D3, Vega-Lite, Observable Plot), data shape tags (daily time series, multi-decade, seasonal, categorical), difficulty (1–4), number of remakes (0–1,200), license, last updated, thumbnail of the finished chart, and a sample dataset. Walter's file: 'fargo_daily_1899_2025.csv', 46,320 rows, columns date, tmax_f, tmin_f, prcp_in, snwd_in, 2.1% missing values. His past searches: 4 this session. Saved recipes: 3 (one marked 'tried, too hard'). Suggested matches for his data shape: 26 recipes, 11 using matplotlib. Related collections curated by members: 'Climate stripes and spirals' (48 recipes), 'Seasonal cycle across decades' (19).

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
